INCIDENT REPORT #IR-2091 -- Cascade Foods Processing Plant, Line 4
Date of incident: 2026-02-11 | Reported by: T. Alvarez, Shift Supervisor

At approximately 14:20, contractor Ben Okafor (employed by Meridian Maintenance Services, not a Cascade Foods employee) was performing scheduled lubrication on the conveyor gearbox on Line 4 when his sleeve caught in an unguarded pinch point. Okafor sustained a laceration to his right forearm requiring 6 stitches at Riverside Urgent Care. He returned to modified duty the same day and did not miss any scheduled shifts. The machine guard for this gearbox had been removed two weeks prior for a bearing replacement and was not reinstalled -- this has been logged as a contributing factor. No Cascade Foods employees were involved in the direct incident, though Line 4 operator M. Kwan witnessed the event and shut down the line immediately.

No chemical exposure occurred. No fire or explosion. The area was dry; this was not a slip/fall incident. PPE (cut-resistant sleeves) was available in the tool crib but was not being worn at the time.

---
From: T. Alvarez
To: safety@cascadefoods.example
Subject: Re: IR-2091 follow-up
Date: 2026-02-12

Hi team, per our call: the missing guard is the root cause. Maintenance has been told to reinstall guards immediately after any service, no exceptions. I've also asked Meridian to confirm their techs are briefed on our PPE rules -- sounds like that briefing didn't happen for Okafor's crew this month.

---
From: D. Ferris, EHS Manager
To: T. Alvarez
Subject: Re: IR-2091 follow-up
Date: 2026-02-13

Agreed. For classification purposes: since Okafor works for Meridian and received treatment beyond first aid (sutures), I'm logging this as a recordable third-party contractor injury on our OSHA-300A-equivalent contractor log, not on Cascade Foods' own employee injury log. It does not count as a Cascade Foods lost-time case since he didn't lose any of his own scheduled shifts with us -- and he's not our employee to begin with. Corrective action (guard reinstallation SOP) is still open, due 2026-02-28.

---
From: Priya Nandakumar, Corporate EHS Director
To: D. Ferris
Subject: Re: IR-2091 follow-up
Date: 2026-02-16

Thanks for the writeup. For our quarterly trending report, can you confirm this is the only pinch-point guarding incident at the Cascade Foods plant level (not just Line 4) in the past 6 months? I want to make sure we're not missing a pattern across other lines before I present to the safety committee next week.

---
From: D. Ferris
To: Priya Nandakumar
Date: 2026-02-16

Confirmed, this is the only guarding-related incident plant-wide in the past 6 months. Lines 1-3 and 5-6 have no similar findings in that window. I'll have the full trending report to you by Friday.

Participants: Ingrid Solberg (Customer, Security Team), Felix Ngata (Anchorpoint Cyber, Solutions Engineer)

Solberg: Let's go through our checklist. First, data residency -- can you guarantee our data stays in the US?
Ngata: For our Standard tier, no -- data may be processed in our US or EU regions depending on load balancing. For the Enterprise tier, yes, we offer a US-only data residency commitment, contractually guaranteed.
Solberg: We'd be on Enterprise. Good. Encryption?
Ngata: Everything is encrypted at rest with AES-256, and in transit with TLS 1.3. That's true across all tiers.
Solberg: Background checks on your engineering staff?
Ngata: Yes, all employees with production access go through a background check as part of onboarding, regardless of tier.
Solberg: SOC 2?
Ngata: We hold SOC 2 Type I, completed last year. We have not yet completed Type II -- that audit is scheduled to start in Q4 2026, results expected mid-2027.
Solberg: Okay, noted as not yet held. Incident response -- what's your SLA for notifying us of a breach?
Ngata: Contractually, 48 hours from confirmed breach for Enterprise customers. For Standard tier it's best-effort with no contractual SLA.
Solberg: And do you carry cyber insurance?
Ngata: Yes, we carry a $5M cyber liability policy.
Solberg: Great. Multi-factor authentication for customer-facing accounts?
Ngata: MFA is available but optional for end users on Standard tier. On Enterprise tier we can enforce it org-wide if you want -- it's off by default until you ask us to turn it on.
Solberg: We'll definitely want that turned on, but as of today it's not on unless we request it, correct?
Ngata: Correct, nothing is turned on automatically -- you'd submit a config request post-contract.
Solberg: Understood. Subprocessors?
Ngata: We maintain a public subprocessor list and notify customers 30 days in advance of adding a new one, with a right to object.
Solberg: One more -- penetration testing?
Ngata: Annual third-party pentest, yes. Last one was March 2026, next one is scheduled March 2027.

[Internal note from Solberg to her manager, forwarded separately: 'Overall solid. Two gaps for our Enterprise contract to close explicitly: SOC 2 Type II isn't done yet, and MFA enforcement needs to be requested -- it won't just happen.']

Solberg: Good to know, noted for our records.

Date: 2026-03-22 | Filed by: Site Safety Officer Yusuf Karimi

At 09:40, apprentice electrician Delphine Aubert (Ironclad employee, 3 months on the job) received an electrical shock while working on a junction box she believed was de-energized.
